sentences.text: Zhuchengceratops was an extinct ceratopsian dinosaur from the family Leptoceratopsidae that lived in modern-day China during the Upper Cretaceous.
It possessed a particularly massive and deep mandible that measured 50 centimeters in length and was thin transversely.
The genus was first described in 2010 by Xing Xu, Kebai Wang, Xijin Zhao, Corwin Sullivan, and Shuqing Chen, with Zhuchengceratops inexpectus as the type species.
Fossils were recovered in 2008 from the Wangshi Group alongside numerous articulated combined bones of the hadrosaurid Shantungosaurus.

The holotype, defined as the specimen the species is based on, is an incomplete articulated skeleton including the combined skull, maxilla, squamosal, jugal, quadrate, wings, outer ring, mandible, the first fourteen vertebrae, ribs, and some additional elements.

Phylogenetic analysis by the authors suggests Zhuchengceratops is an advanced leptoceratopsid more closely related to Leptoceratops and Udanoceratops, although the internal relationships of this triplet remain unresolved.
Zhuchengceratops lived during the late Cretaceous period, approximately 75 million years ago in the Campanian stage, in what is now Asia.
